answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation blog post dated 2026-07-01 (party statement, company-published), with quoted statements from Sharon AI CEO James Manning and Firmus co-CEO Tim Rosenfield as relayed in that post.
answer.note: NVIDIA states it is introducing a business model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure to serve AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, supported by revenue-sharing and credit-support terms. NVIDIA says it would earn both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity, which it describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. This is a company description of a new commercial structure, not a reported result, so it supports the conclusion that NVDA is pursuing a model that adds usage-linked revenue on top of hardware sales, subject to how the terms are implemented. Firmus's Batam, Indonesia DSX AI factory campus, described as expected to scale to 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs, is a forward-looking plan stated in an NVIDIA release; it is a supply and demand lead for NVIDIA GPU volume in that campus, not a confirmed purchase order or a dated delivery schedule. Sharon AI and Firmus are relevant as AI cloud channel partners that would procure or deploy NVIDIA infrastructure under the model, but the source does not state their purchase amounts or contract values.
limitations: The source gives no quantified revenue-share percentage, credit-support amount, contract duration, or the financial size of the new model for NVIDIA.
The source does not state whether the Sharon AI or Firmus arrangements are signed, funded or binding; their participation is described only through partner statements and plans.
The Firmus campus figures of 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs are expected or maximum values with no completion date, phasing, or confirmed GPU purchase schedule.
The source does not identify which AI clouds other than Sharon AI and Firmus are using the model, so the breadth of adoption is unknown.
The source is a company promotional release, so its characterization of adoption and recurring earnings is management framing without independent verification.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's next 10-Q or 10-K and earnings call materials for any disclosure of revenue-sharing, cloud-revenue share, or credit-support arrangements and any quantified exposure.
Check Firmus and Sharon AI public announcements or filings for signed agreements, financing, and phased timelines for the Batam campus and sovereign AI compute projects.
Check whether NVIDIA discloses any credit guarantees, financing commitments, or contingent obligations tied to AI cloud partners in filing footnotes.
